requirements.text: Students should be able to search the catalogue easily with filtering options by title, author, or subject, and see real-time availability.
Students must be able to borrow, return, and renew items online without needing to stand in line at the library desk.
Students should have a personal dashboard displaying current loans, outstanding fines, reservation history, alerts, and quick actions.
The system should provide automated email reminders for upcoming due dates and outstanding fines.
Students should be able to book study rooms online, view available slots, choose the size of the room, and confirm bookings.
Staff should have tools to add, update, and retire catalogue items easily.
Staff should have advanced search functionalities to locate specific items or groups within the inventory.
The system should allow for bulk actions to update the status of multiple items at once.
Staff should have access to detailed usage reports providing insights into loan volumes, popular items, and room utilization.
The system should notify staff when items are running low or frequently checked out.
The library management system must integrate smoothly with the university’s existing systems, like the student record system.
The system must handle the volume of users effectively, especially during peak times.
The system must provide robust security measures to comply with GDPR regarding the handling of student data.
There should be training and support provided for both staff and students during the transition to the new system.
